def: Python's real-number type: a 64-bit IEEE 754 double stored as a 24-byte object, accurate to about 15 to 16 significant digits.
The 64-bit floating-point format with a 53-bit significand, which gives roughly 15 to 16 decimal digits.
The gap between 1.0 and the next representable float above it (about 2.2e-16 for doubles), which sets the best relative accuracy.
Rewriting a per-element loop as one operation on a whole array so that compiled code runs the loop.
A number stored as a separate heap object with a header, as every Python int and float is, rather than as raw bytes.
The sum of the products of matching entries of two equal-length vectors, such as 1x4 + 2x5 + 3x6 = 32.
A way of adding floats that tracks the rounding error of each step and feeds it back, so long sums stay accurate.
Of an operation, giving the same result however the terms are grouped; real addition is, but floating-point addition is not.
A single expression, such as [f(x) for x in xs], that builds a list from another iterable.
Two names referring to the same mutable object, so a change through one name is visible through the other.
